items.answer: z₁. O₁ lies on that axis.
items.rationale: (concept, targets the off-by-one misconception M3: "Joint i rotates about zᵢ, and its position is Oᵢ.") Tests: whether the learner links joint i to frame i−1. A learner who answers "z₂ and O₂" will build every Jacobian column from the wrong joint.

items.answer:
⁰z₀ = ⁰z₁ = (0, 0, 1)
⁰O₁ = (a₁c₁, a₁s₁, 0)
⁰O₂ = (a₁c₁ + a₂c₁₂, a₁s₁ + a₂s₁₂, 0)
items.rationale: (computation) Tests: composing transforms and reading off positions. It is also the exact set of inputs for the first Jacobian example. Learners who write O₂ = (a₂c₂, a₂s₂, 0) are mixing up local and base frames.

items.answer: Joint 3 acts about z₂, so compute ⁰T₂ = ⁰T₁ · ¹T₂. The third column of its rotation block gives ⁰z₂, and its position column gives ⁰O₂.
